overview: This 105-page file documents U.S. efforts from 1940 to 1944 to assess Japan’s industrial capacity, economic mobilization, and strategic vulnerabilities. Drawing on diplomatic reporting, FBI and military intelligence, confidential informants, translated Japanese and German press, corporate information, and factory directories, it traces Japan’s pursuit of economic self-sufficiency and increasingly centralized wartime control over investment, labor, transport, banking, raw materials, and production. Its coverage ranges from broad surveys of metals, mining, chemicals, fuels, electric power, shipbuilding, aircraft production, and railways to detailed intelligence on individual companies, copper facilities, shipyards, ports, and industrial sites in Japan and its empire.
interest: Japan's wartime industry via fragmented American intelligence: interviews, press translations, German reports, and evidence of shortages, congestion and dispersal.
